The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.
Summary of Restricted Stock Unit Activity
At the end of 2024, 7,278,000 shares were available to be granted as RSUs, and the following awards, adjusted for the effects of the special
dividend, were outstanding:
• 2,677,000 time-based RSUs, which vest upon continued employment or service over specified periods of time; and
• 122,000 performance-based RSUs, of which 95,000 were granted to executive officers subject to the determination of the attainment of
performance targets for 2024, which occurred in September 2024. At that time, depending upon long-service terms, at least 33% of the
units vested. The remaining awards vest upon continued employment over specified periods of time. Please refer to Note 1 for
accelerated vesting requirements.

Short-Term Borrowings
The Company maintains various short-term bank credit facilities, with a borrowing capacity of $1,198 and $1,234, in 2024 and 2023. Short-term
borrowings outstanding were immaterial at the end of 2024 and 2023.
Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

Our members may utilize their memberships at all of our warehouses and e-commerce sites. Gold Star memberships are available to individuals;
Business memberships are limited to businesses, including individuals with a business license, retail sales license, or comparable document.
Business members may add additional cardholders (affiliates), to which the same annual fee applies. Affiliates are not available for Gold Star
members. During fiscal 2024, our annual fee for these memberships was $60 in the U.S. and varies in other countries. All paid memberships
include a free household card.
Paid members (except affiliates) were eligible to upgrade to an Executive membership in the U.S., for an additional annual fee of $60. Executive
memberships are also available in Canada, Mexico, the U.K., Japan, Korea, Taiwan, and Australia, for which the additional fee varies. Executive
members earn a 2% reward on qualified purchases (generally up to a maximum reward of $1,000 per year), redeemable at Costco warehouses.
The sales penetration of Executive members represented approximately 73.3% of worldwide net sales in 2024.
Our member renewal rate was 92.9% in the U.S. and Canada and 90.5% worldwide at the end of 2024. The majority of members renew within
six months following their renewal date. Our renewal rate, which excludes affiliates of Business members, is a trailing calculation that captures
renewals during the period seven to eighteen months prior to the reporting date. Our membership counts include active memberships as well as
memberships that have not renewed within the 12 months prior to the reporting date.

Goodwill represents the excess of acquisition cost over the fair value of the net assets acquired and is not subject to amortization. The Company
reviews goodwill annually in the fourth quarter for impairment or when circumstances indicate carrying value may exceed the fair value. This
evaluation is performed at the reporting unit level. If a qualitative assessment indicates that it is more likely than not that the fair value is less
than carrying value, a quantitative analysis is completed using either the income or market approach, or a combination of both. The income
approach estimates fair value based on expected discounted future cash flows, while the market approach uses comparable public companies
and transactions to develop metrics to be applied to historical and expected future operating results.

The Company is currently under audit by several jurisdictions in the United States and abroad. Some audits may conclude in the next 12
months, and the unrecognized tax benefits recorded in relation to the audits may differ from actual settlement amounts. It is not practical to
estimate the effect, if any, of any amount of such change during the next 12 months to previously recorded uncertain tax positions in connection

* Depreciation and Amortization: $2,237 million
* Non-cash Lease Expense: $315 million
* Stock-based Compensation: $818 million

Total Adjusted EBITDA = Net Income + (Depreciation & Amortization) + (Non-cash Lease Expense) + (Stock-based Compensation)

Adjusted EBITDA for 2024 = $7,367 million + $2,237 million + $315 million + $818 million = **$10,737 million** or approximately $10.7 billion.

To compute the adjusted EBITDA Margin for 2024, we first need to calculate the EBITDA (Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation, and Amortization).

1. Calculate EBITDA:
   - Net Income Attributable to Costco: $7,367 million
   - Provision for income taxes: $2,373 million
   - Interest expense: Not provided in the data, but we can calculate it as follows:
     - Interest income and other, net: $624 million
     - Total interest (expense + income): $169 million (from operating expenses) + $624 million = $793 million (estimated)
   - Depreciation and amortization: $2,237 million

2. EBITDA Calculation:
   - EBITDA = Net Income Attributable to Costco + Provision for income taxes + Interest expense - Interest income and other, net + Depreciation and amortization
   - However, since we don't have the exact interest expense, we will use the estimated total interest (expense + income) of $793 million as a proxy.
   - EBITDA = $7,367 million + $2,373 million + $793 million - $624 million + $2,237 million
   - EBITDA = $10,058 million

3. Calculate Adjusted EBITDA Margin:
   - Operating income: $9,285 million
   - EBITDA: $10,058 million (using the estimated total interest)
   - Adjusted EBITDA Margin = EBITDA / Operating income * 100%
   - Adjusted EBITDA Margin = ($10,058 million) / ($9,285 million) * 100%
   - Adjusted EBITDA Margin ≈ 107.3%

However, since the provided data does not include the exact interest expense, this calculation is an estimate. The actual adjusted EBITDA margin may vary depending on the accurate interest expense figure.

To determine the EV/EBITDA ratio for 2024, we need to estimate Enterprise Value (EV) and EBITDA using the market value of equity and other financial data from the provided context. Here's how to calculate it:

**Step 1: Calculate Market Value of Equity:**

* From the "Equity" section of the Consolidated Balance Sheets for September 1, 2024:
    * Total shareholders' equity (net of non-controlling interests) = $23,622 million
    * Total common stock issued and outstanding = 443,126,000 shares
* Market Value of Equity = Total Shareholders' Equity / Total Common Stock Issued and Outstanding
Market Value of Equity = $23,622 million / 443,126,000 shares ≈ $53.29 per share

**Step 2: Calculate Total Debt and Cash:**

* From the Consolidated Balance Sheets:
    * Total long-term debt (excluding current portion) = $5,794 million
    * Cash and cash equivalents = $9,906 million

**Step 3: Estimate Enterprise Value (EV):**

* EV ≈ Market Value of Equity + Total Debt - Excess Cash
* We don't have explicit information about excess cash. For simplicity, let's assume the excess cash is negligible compared to debt and equity. Therefore, we'll approximate EV using just market value of equity and total debt:

    * EV ≈ $53.29 per share * 443,126,000 shares + $5,794 million
    * EV ≈ $23,622 million + $5,794 million = $29,416 million

**Step 4: Calculate EBITDA:**

* From the Consolidated Statements of Income for 2024 (amounts in millions):
    * Operating income = $9,285 million
    * Depreciation and amortization = $2,237 million
    * EBITDA ≈ Operating Income + Depreciation and Amortization
    * EBITDA = $9,285 million + $2,237 million = $11,522 million

**Step 5: Calculate EV/EBITDA Ratio:**

* EV/EBITDA Ratio = EV / EBITDA
* Using the approximate EV calculated above and the 2024 EBITDA:

    * EV/EBITDA Ratio ≈ $29,416 million / $11,522 million ≈ 2.55x

**Important Notes:**

1. This is a simplified calculation due to the lack of explicit excess cash information. In a real-world scenario, you would need to accurately estimate excess cash to get a more precise EV.
2. The diluted shares outstanding for 2024 are not provided in the context. Using basic shares outstanding might lead to an overestimation of the ratio.


Therefore, based on this simplified calculation, the estimated EV/EBITDA ratio for Costco Wholesale Corporation in 2024 is approximately **2.55x**.

To calculate Enterprise Value (EV) for 2024 using the market value of equity, we need to first determine the fully diluted shares outstanding, which is already provided as 444,759 thousands.

Step 1: Calculate Market Value of Equity (MVE):
The MVE can be calculated using the total equity and the number of issued shares. From the Balance Sheet data for September 1, 2024:
- Total Equity = $23,622 million
- Common Stock shares outstanding = 443,126 thousands (or approximately 443.13 million)

MVE = Total Equity + Additional Paid-in Capital - Accumulated Other Comprehensive Loss
MVE = $23,622 + $7,829 - $1,828
MVE ≈ $30,623 million (or approximately 30.62 billion)

Step 2: Calculate Enterprise Value:
Enterprise Value (EV) is calculated as the sum of Market Value of Equity and Total Debt minus Excess Cash (non-operating asset). However, since we are only provided with excess cash information for the year, we will use it to calculate EV.

Total Debt (from Balance Sheet data):
- Long-term debt (excluding current portion) = $5,794 million
- Current portion of long-term debt = $103 million
Total Debt ≈ $5,897 million

Excess Cash (assuming it's part of Total Current Assets or Other Current Assets):
- Cash and cash equivalents = $9,906 million
- Short-term investments = $1,238 million
- Receivables, net = $2,721 million
- Merchandise inventories = $18,647 million
- Other current assets = $1,734 million
Excess Cash ≈ $9,906 + $1,238 - $2,721 - $18,647 - $1,734 (assuming it's a small amount) ≈ $-3,548 million
Note: For simplicity and as per the problem statement, we will assume Excess Cash is zero for this calculation.

EV = MVE + Total Debt - Excess Cash (or 0 in this case)
EV = $30,623 + $5,897 ≈ $36,520 million (or approximately 36.52 billion)

Therefore, the calculated Enterprise Value for 2024 is approximately $36,520 million.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.
Summary of Restricted Stock Unit Activity
At the end of 2024, 7,278,000 shares were available to be granted as RSUs, and the following awards, adjusted for the effects of the special
dividend, were outstanding:
• 2,677,000 time-based RSUs, which vest upon continued employment or service over specified periods of time; and
• 122,000 performance-based RSUs, of which 95,000 were granted to executive officers subject to the determination of the attainment of
performance targets for 2024, which occurred in September 2024. At that time, depending upon long-service terms, at least 33% of the
units vested. The remaining awards vest upon continued employment over specified periods of time. Please refer to Note 1 for
accelerated vesting requirements.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

Our members may utilize their memberships at all of our warehouses and e-commerce sites. Gold Star memberships are available to individuals;
Business memberships are limited to businesses, including individuals with a business license, retail sales license, or comparable document.
Business members may add additional cardholders (affiliates), to which the same annual fee applies. Affiliates are not available for Gold Star
members. During fiscal 2024, our annual fee for these memberships was $60 in the U.S. and varies in other countries. All paid memberships
include a free household card.
Paid members (except affiliates) were eligible to upgrade to an Executive membership in the U.S., for an additional annual fee of $60. Executive
memberships are also available in Canada, Mexico, the U.K., Japan, Korea, Taiwan, and Australia, for which the additional fee varies. Executive
members earn a 2% reward on qualified purchases (generally up to a maximum reward of $1,000 per year), redeemable at Costco warehouses.
The sales penetration of Executive members represented approximately 73.3% of worldwide net sales in 2024.
Our member renewal rate was 92.9% in the U.S. and Canada and 90.5% worldwide at the end of 2024. The majority of members renew within
six months following their renewal date. Our renewal rate, which excludes affiliates of Business members, is a trailing calculation that captures
renewals during the period seven to eighteen months prior to the reporting date. Our membership counts include active memberships as well as
memberships that have not renewed within the 12 months prior to the reporting date.

Goodwill represents the excess of acquisition cost over the fair value of the net assets acquired and is not subject to amortization. The Company
reviews goodwill annually in the fourth quarter for impairment or when circumstances indicate carrying value may exceed the fair value. This
evaluation is performed at the reporting unit level. If a qualitative assessment indicates that it is more likely than not that the fair value is less
than carrying value, a quantitative analysis is completed using either the income or market approach, or a combination of both. The income
approach estimates fair value based on expected discounted future cash flows, while the market approach uses comparable public companies
and transactions to develop metrics to be applied to historical and expected future operating results.

### 1. **Identify Relevant Financial Metrics**
The formula for WACC is:

WACC = (Cost of Equity * Weights of Equity) + (Cost of Debt * Weights of Debt)

Where:
- Cost of Equity is typically calculated using the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM): 
   Cost of Equity = Risk-Free Rate + Beta * (Market Return - Risk-Free Rate)
- Cost of Debt can be derived from the company's interest expenses and debt levels.

### 3. **Weights of Equity and Debt**
These weights are typically obtained from the company's capital structure, i.e., the proportion of equity and debt in their total capital.

### 4. **Calculate WACC**
Once you have all these values, plug them into the WACC formula to arrive at the company's weighted average cost of capital for 2024.

income tax rate in future periods is $79 and $14 at the end of 2024 and 2023.

penalties recognized during 2024 and 2023, and accrued at the end of each respective period were immaterial.

months, and the unrecognized tax benefits recorded in relation to the audits may differ from actual settlement amounts. It is not practical to
estimate the effect, if any, of any amount of such change during the next 12 months to previously recorded uncertain tax positions in connection
with the audits. The Company does not anticipate that there will be a material increase or decrease in the total amount of unrecognized tax
benefits in the next 12 months.

approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

To determine the operating cash tax rate in 2024, we need to calculate the effective tax rate and then divide it by the operating cash flow.

Step 1: Calculate the effective tax rate
The company's income before taxes is $9,740 million. The provision for income taxes is $2,373 million.
The effective tax rate can be calculated as follows:
Effective Tax Rate = (Provision for Income Taxes / Income Before Taxes) * 100
Effective Tax Rate = ($2,373 / $9,740) * 100
Effective Tax Rate = 24.4%

Step 2: Calculate the operating cash flow
The company's net income is $7,367 million. The adjustments to reconcile net income to net cash provided by operating activities are as follows:
Depreciation and amortization = $2,237 million
Non-cash lease expense = $315 million
Stock-based compensation = $818 million
Impairment of assets and other non-cash operating activities, net = ($9) million
Changes in operating assets and liabilities = $741 million
Net cash provided by operating activities = $11,339 million
Operating Cash Flow = Net Cash Provided by Operating Activities / Effective Tax Rate
Operating Cash Flow = $11,339 / 0.244
Operating Cash Flow ≈ $46,582 million

Step 3: Calculate the operating cash tax rate
The operating cash tax rate can be calculated as follows:
Operating Cash Tax Rate = (Effective Tax Rate / Total Revenue) * 100
However, since we are looking for the operating cash tax rate in 2024, we should calculate it using the net income and total revenue of 2024.
Operating Cash Tax Rate (2024) = (Provision for Income Taxes / Net Income) * 100
Operating Cash Tax Rate (2024) = ($2,373 / $7,367) * 100
However, the above calculation is incorrect because we should calculate it using the total revenue of 2024.
Total Revenue = Net Sales + Membership Fees
Total Revenue = $249,625 million + $4,828 million
Total Revenue = $254,453 million
Operating Cash Tax Rate (2024) = ($2,373 / $254,453) * 100
Operating Cash Tax Rate (2024) ≈ 0.93%

Note: The operating cash tax rate is usually expressed as a percentage of total revenue or net income. However, in this case, we calculated it using the effective tax rate and total revenue, which might not be the standard method.

To calculate the Unlevered Beta for 2024, we need to consider the following information:

1. The Market Return is given as 11%.
2. The Cost of Debt is 6%.
3. The Price of Costco Stock is $940.
4. The Beta for Costco (Levered) can be found in the text, which is 0.79.
5. We need to find the Unlevered Beta.

The formula to calculate the Unlevered Beta is:

Unlevered Beta = Levered Beta / (1 - (Cost of Debt / Market Return))

First, we need to calculate the denominator:

1 - (Cost of Debt / Market Return) = 1 - (0.06 / 0.11) = 1 - 0.545 = 0.455

Now, we can calculate the Unlevered Beta:

Unlevered Beta = Levered Beta / (1 - (Cost of Debt / Market Return))
= 0.79 / 0.455
= 1.73

Therefore, the Unlevered Beta for 2024 is approximately 1.73.

To determine Invested Capital including Goodwill for 2024, we need to calculate the following:

1. Total Debt (Long-Term Debt + Short-Term Debt)
2. Cash and Cash Equivalents
3. Total Equity (Total Shareholders' Equity)
4. Subtract Total Debt from Cash and Cash Equivalents + Total Equity
5. Add Goodwill to the result in step 4

Based on the provided financial statements, here are the calculations:

1. **Total Debt:**
   - Long-term debt: $5,794 (from the Consolidated Balance Sheets)
   - Short-term debt: Not explicitly mentioned in the provided data, but can be calculated as follows:
     - Total current liabilities: $35,464
     - Current portion of long-term debt: $103
     - Other current liabilities: $6,210
     - Accounts payable: $19,421
     - Accrued salaries and benefits: $4,794
     - Accrued member rewards: $2,435
     - Deferred membership fees: $2,501
     - Short-term debt = Total current liabilities - (Current portion of long-term debt + Other current liabilities)
     - Short-term debt ≈ $28,679

   - Total Debt = Long-term debt + Short-term debt
   - Total Debt ≈ $5,794 + $28,679 (approximation)
   - Total Debt ≈ $34,473

2. **Cash and Cash Equivalents:**
   - Cash and cash equivalents: $9,906 (from the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows)

3. **Total Equity:**
   - Total Shareholders' Equity: $23,622 (from the Consolidated Balance Sheets)
4. **Invested Capital including Goodwill:**
   - Invested Capital = Cash and Cash Equivalents + Total Debt - Total Equity + Goodwill
   - Since Goodwill is not explicitly mentioned as a separate number, we can assume it is included in the "Other long-term assets" section of the Consolidated Balance Sheets, which has a value of $3,936.

   - Invested Capital = $9,906 + $34,473 - $23,622 + $3,936
   - Invested Capital ≈ $15,693

Therefore, the Invested Capital including Goodwill for 2024 is approximately $15,693 million.

amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

dividend, were outstanding:

• 122,000 performance-based RSUs, of which 95,000 were granted to executive officers subject to the determination of the attainment of
performance targets for 2024, which occurred in September 2024. At that time, depending upon long-service terms, at least 33% of the
units vested. The remaining awards vest upon continued employment over specified periods of time. Please refer to Note 1 for

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

Our members may utilize their memberships at all of our warehouses and e-commerce sites. Gold Star memberships are available to individuals;
Business memberships are limited to businesses, including individuals with a business license, retail sales license, or comparable document.
Business members may add additional cardholders (affiliates), to which the same annual fee applies. Affiliates are not available for Gold Star
members. During fiscal 2024, our annual fee for these memberships was $60 in the U.S. and varies in other countries. All paid memberships
include a free household card.
Paid members (except affiliates) were eligible to upgrade to an Executive membership in the U.S., for an additional annual fee of $60. Executive
memberships are also available in Canada, Mexico, the U.K., Japan, Korea, Taiwan, and Australia, for which the additional fee varies. Executive
members earn a 2% reward on qualified purchases (generally up to a maximum reward of $1,000 per year), redeemable at Costco warehouses.
The sales penetration of Executive members represented approximately 73.3% of worldwide net sales in 2024.
Our member renewal rate was 92.9% in the U.S. and Canada and 90.5% worldwide at the end of 2024. The majority of members renew within
six months following their renewal date. Our renewal rate, which excludes affiliates of Business members, is a trailing calculation that captures
renewals during the period seven to eighteen months prior to the reporting date. Our membership counts include active memberships as well as
memberships that have not renewed within the 12 months prior to the reporting date.

Goodwill represents the excess of acquisition cost over the fair value of the net assets acquired and is not subject to amortization. The Company
reviews goodwill annually in the fourth quarter for impairment or when circumstances indicate carrying value may exceed the fair value. This
evaluation is performed at the reporting unit level. If a qualitative assessment indicates that it is more likely than not that the fair value is less
than carrying value, a quantitative analysis is completed using either the income or market approach, or a combination of both. The income
approach estimates fair value based on expected discounted future cash flows, while the market approach uses comparable public companies
and transactions to develop metrics to be applied to historical and expected future operating results.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

The Company maintains various short-term bank credit facilities, with a borrowing capacity of $1,198 and $1,234, in 2024 and 2023. Short-term

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate

are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

1. **Calculate Net Income Before Noncontrolling Interests**:
   - From the Consolidated Statements of Income, Net income including noncontrolling interests is $7,367 million.
   - Since the net income attributable to noncontrolling interests is not provided, we will use the total net income as a proxy for Net income before noncontrolling interests.

2. **Calculate Taxes**:
   - Provision for income taxes is $2,373 million.
   - Income before income taxes is $9,740 million.

3. **Calculate NOPAT**:
   - NOPAT = (Net income before noncontrolling interests) * (1 - Tax rate)
   - Tax rate is calculated as the Provision for income taxes / Income before income taxes = 24.4%.
   - NOPAT = $7,367 million * (1 - 0.244) = $5,519 million

Therefore, the estimated NOPAT for 2024 is $5,519 million.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

warehouses opened in 2023 and 2024, partially offset by the impact of one less week of sales in 2024. Sales increased $10,639, or 6% in core
merchandise categories, increasing in all categories. Sales increased $1,276, or 3% in warehouse ancillary and other businesses, led by
pharmacy, partially offset by a decrease in gasoline.
During 2024, the volume of gasoline sold increased approximately 1%, positively impacting net sales by $400, or 17 basis points, which includes
the impact of one less week of sales in 2024. Lower gasoline prices negatively impacted net sales by $917, or 39 basis points, compared to
2023, with a 3% decrease in the average price per gallon. Changes in foreign currencies relative to the U.S. dollar negatively impacted net sales
by approximately $474, 20 basis points, compared to 2023, attributable to our Canadian and Other International operations.
Comparable Sales
Comparable sales increased 5% during 2024 and were positively impacted by an increase in shopping frequency, partially offset by a slight
decrease in average ticket.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.
On May 18, 2024, the Company paid the $1,000 outstanding principal balance and interest on the 2.750% Senior Notes using cash and cash
equivalents and short-term investments.

The 2019 Incentive Plan authorized the issuance of 17,500,000 shares (10,000,000 RSUs) of common stock for future grants, plus the
remaining shares that were available for grant and the future forfeited shares from grants under the previous plan, up to a maximum aggregate
of 27,800,000 shares (15,885,000 RSUs). The Company issues new shares of common stock upon vesting of RSUs. Shares for vested RSUs
are generally delivered to participants annually, net of shares withheld for taxes.
As required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, in conjunction with the 2024 special dividend, the number of shares subject to outstanding RSUs was
increased on the dividend record date to preserve their value. They were adjusted by multiplying the number of outstanding shares by a factor of
1.018, representing the ratio of the Nasdaq closing price of $674.62 on December 26, 2023, which was the last trading day immediately prior to
the ex-dividend date, to the Nasdaq opening price of $662.70 on the ex-dividend date, December 27, 2023. The outstanding RSUs increased by
approximately 52,000. The adjustment did not result in additional stock-based compensation expense, as the fair value of the awards did not
change. As further required by the 2019 Incentive Plan, the maximum number of shares issuable under the plan was proportionally adjusted,
which resulted in an additional 128,000 RSU shares available to be granted.

Long-Term Debt
The Company's long-term debt consists primarily of Senior Notes, described below. The Company at its option may redeem the Senior Notes at
any time, in whole or in part, at a redemption price plus accrued interest. The redemption price is equal to the greater of 100% of the principal
amount or the sum of the present value of the remaining scheduled payments of principal and interest to maturity. Additionally, upon certain
events, a holder has the right to require a repurchase at a price of 101% of the principal amount plus accrued and unpaid interest. Interest on all
outstanding long-term debt is payable semi-annually. The estimated fair value of Senior Notes is valued using Level 2 inputs.
Other long-term debt consists of Guaranteed Senior Notes issued by the Company's Japanese subsidiary, valued using Level 3 inputs. In
November 2023, the Company’s Japan subsidiary issued four Guaranteed Senior Notes, totaling approximately $500, at fixed interest rates
ranging from 1.400% to 2.120%. Interest is payable semi-annually, and maturity dates range from November 7, 2033, to November 7, 2043. In
July 2024, the Japanese subsidiary repaid $77 of its Guaranteed Senior Notes.

1. Calculate EBITA (Earnings Before Interest and Taxes) for 2024.
2. Determine the total interest expense for 2024.
3. Divide the EBITA by the total interest expense.

Step 1: Calculate EBITA for 2024
EBITA = Operating income + Other income (expense) - Interest income and other, net + Interest expense
From the provided data:
Operating income in 2024 = $9,285
Other income (expense) in 2024 = $624 (interest income) + $-169 (interest expense), but since we are calculating EBITA, interest income is not subtracted as it is positive. However, we need to add back the net interest expense from interest income and other expenses if it's negative. In this case, it's a negative number, so we'll consider the negative value of interest expense in the calculation for clarity:
Interest expense in 2024 = $169 (negative due to other income) + $-160 (from operating income) - $624 (interest income) = $-575 However, since we are calculating EBITA, we will use the absolute value of interest expenses.
Interest expense in 2024 = $169
Therefore, EBITA = $9,285 + $624 - $169 = $9,740

Step 2: Determine the total interest expense for 2024
Total interest expense for 2024 = $169 (from operating income)

Step 3: Calculate EBITA Interest Coverage Ratio for 2024
EBITA Interest Coverage Ratio = EBITA / Total interest expense
= $9,740 / $169
= 57.68
